channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Bond Market Selloff: Are Surging Yields a Threat to the Global Stock Rally?
item.description: In equity markets, the myth goes that the only way is up. That perception has gained traction as global stock prices have largely ignored the selloff in bond markets. Yields on long-dated government debt have surged to near two-decade highs as investors worry about whether inflation and fiscal deficits can be tamed, and as sovereign bonds compete with an AI-fueled corporate borrowing boom.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Jaisinghani, Alice Gledhill and Margaryta Kirakosian

item.title: Oil Extends Advance as US-Iran Escalation Revives Hormuz Risks
item.description: Oil rose for a second session as fresh hostilities between the US and Iran raised concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, where crude carriers were hit by projectiles. Leslie Palti-Guzman, Founder at Energy Vista, discusses the outlook for global energy as conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt flow. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Uruguay acelera desdolarización con nuevos fondos Money Market
item.description: Los inversores en Uruguay están colocando una mayor parte de su patrimonio en fondos Money Market y bonos del gobierno en pesos, lo que da un mayor impulso a los esfuerzos de este país sudamericano, considerado un refugio seguro, por reducir su dependencia del dólar.
item.dc:creator: Ken Parks

item.title: Wells Fargo Analysts Join JPMorgan Traders in Turning Cautious on US Stocks
item.description: Wells Fargo & Co. is the second bank to turn cautious on US stocks this week as the market heads into what is historically the worst month on the calendar for equities and upcoming midterm elections add to uncertainty surrounding the artificial-intelligence trade.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: EU Considers Front-Loading Ukraine Loan as Funding Shortage Hits
item.description: European Union member states are considering accelerating payments from the bloc’s €90 billion ($104 billion) loan to Ukraine as Kyiv faces a funding crunch, the bloc’s rotating presidency said.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano and Olivia Fletcher

item.title: Partners Group CEO Rejects Redemption Concerns
item.description: Partners Group CEO David Layton joined Bloomberg Open Interest to push back on concerns that his move to CIO signals trouble at the private-markets giant. He explains why the leadership shake-up isn’t tied to redemption pressure, says the firm is gaining fundraising share despite an industry slowdown, and reveals why elevated evergreen-fund redemptions could continue for another 12 to 18 months. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Redwire is Growing Strawberries in Space
item.description: Redwire CEO Peter Cannito joins Bloomberg Open Interest to break down the next phase of the space economy—from orbital data centers and cheaper space manufacturing to the growing US, China space race. He also explains why falling transportation costs, SpaceX partnerships and even space agriculture could create major new commercial opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Senegal, IMF Reach Staff Agreement on $2.2 Billion Loan Program
item.description: Senegal and the International Monetary Fund reached a preliminary deal for a program that will resume lending to the West African nation, two years after funding was frozen following the discovery of billions of dollars of previously hidden loans.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Höije and Jorgelina do Rosario

item.title: The Coming Shakeout in Private Credit
item.description: Achilles Global Management CIO and Founder Sachin Khajuria says private credit is entering a decade-long shakeout as higher rates expose weaker managers and drive a flight to quality. He joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why private markets could emerge stronger and warns retail investors moving into private assets to closely examine liquidity, transparency and risk. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Surveillance 9/1/2026
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: David Booth on His Book and Historic KU Athletics Donation
item.description: David Booth, Dimensional Fund Advisors founder and Chairman, discusses the theme of his new book "Stay Calm: Learn to Embrace Uncertainty in Investing and Life," and his historic $300 Million gift to the University of Kansas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Fall as Oil Jump Fuels Fed-Hike Bets
item.description: A renewed drop in bonds reduced bets on riskier corners of Wall Street, hitting stocks on worries that elevated oil prices will fuel inflation and force the Federal Reserve to lift rates. Jordan Jackson, Global Market Strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, discusses the markets and his outlook on inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wells Fargo, Barclays Backed Collapsed Headlam With £85 Million
item.description: Wells Fargo & Co. and Barclays Plc provided as much as £85 million ($115 million) to Headlam Group Plc just months before the British flooring distributor appointed insolvency officials.
item.dc:creator: Constantine Courcoulas and Tuhin Kar

item.title: Gap Up on Leadership Shift; Shein's Market Debut | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Gap (GAP) shares jumped after naming a retail industry veteran to head Old Navy and profit outpaced estimates, offsetting a sales decline at the value chain and lower sales guidance. - Apple's (AAPL) Tim Cook handed over the reins to John Ternus on Tuesday, capping a tenure as chief executive officer that cemented the company as an iconic global brand and turned its stock into one of the most reliable bets. - Shein Global Holdings’ shares long-awaited market debut has come at an awkward time: the fast-fashion retailer’s peak growth years are behind it just as tariffs, regulatory pressure and intensifying competition are making its next phase harder. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China’s Real Estate Market Enters the ‘Resale’ Era
item.description: A big moment for Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: Peru Inflation Just Tops Estimate to Hit Fastest Since 2023
item.description: Inflation in Peru’s capital accelerated slightly more than expected in August, hitting the fastest pace in almost three years, pressured by housing and utilities including electricity and gas.
item.dc:creator: Carla Samon Ros

item.title: Saudi Arabia Gets Over $12 Billion in Offers for Bond Sale
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s dollar-bond sale has drawn in offers exceeding $12 billion, a sign that demand for the country’s debt remains healthy despite the economic strain caused by the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Mirette Magdy

item.title: US-Iran Tensions High After Strikes on Two Tankers in Hormuz
item.description: US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz heightened after a flurry of military strikes at the start of the week, with neither side prepared to cede ground over the crucial waterway.
item.dc:creator: Grant Smith, Weilun Soon and Eltaf Najafizada

item.title: Stocks Fall as Oil Jump Keeps Bond Yields Elevated: Markets Wrap
item.description: A fresh bout of bond volatility left traders unwilling to make riskier bets, with stocks falling on worries that an oil rally will fuel inflation and force the Federal Reserve to lift rates.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Citadel Says Marshall Wace ‘Stonewalling’ in Spat Over Shatz
item.description: Citadel accused Marshall Wace of failing to adhere to a court order to hand over documents relating to the British hedge fund group’s recruitment of former Citadel portfolio manager Daniel Shatz as its global credit head.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch
